extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent owners and third‑party requesters (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for handling ex parte reexamination requests under 35 U.S.C. 302–305, including how to decide grant/deny, preserve review rights, handle patent owner statements and amendments, and format submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper grounds for reexamination (102(c) / first-to-invent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds based on 35 U.S.C. 102(c) for reexamination proceedings examined under the first-to-invent prior art regime are improper for reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302 and are not considered or commented upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should note such grounds are improper and not consider them. See 37 CFR 1.552(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of electronic correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: For electronic transmissions, correspondence (except for a request for reexamination and a corrected or replacement request) will be considered timely filed if (a) transmitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system in accordance with 37 CFR 1.6(a)(4), and (b) includes a certificate of transmission for each piece of correspondence stating the date of transmission, which is prior to the expiration of the set period of time in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include and retain certificate of transmission showing date prior to expiration of time period in the Office action; follow 37 CFR 1.6(a)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to grant or deny reexamination — panel review and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing a decision on the request for reexamination, the examiner will prepare for and set up a panel review conference per MPEP §2271.01; if the conference confirms the examiner's preliminary decision to grant or deny reexamination, the decision will be completed and signed by the examiner, with two or more conferees initialing the action to indicate their presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may prepare the decision and, where applicable, the first Office action before or after the conference and revise as needed. Use transmittal form PTOL‑465 to forward copies to third‑party requester when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving right to Board review of SNQ (requester/patent owner reconsideration requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve the right to have the Board review the substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) issue, a patent owner must first request reconsideration of the SNQ determination before the examiner (e.g., in a patent owner's statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or in a response under 37 CFR 1.111) and then seek review before the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the appeal brief present the SNQ issue and arguments under a separate heading and identify the communication in which reconsideration was first requested. For ex parte reexamination ordered on or after June 25, 2010, failure to request reconsideration before the examiner forfeits Board review of the SNQ issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging reexamination order as ultra vires (37 CFR 1.181(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.181(a)(3) to vacate an ex parte reexamination order as 'ultra vires' is available only where the USPTO acted in 'brazen defiance' of its statutory authorization in granting the order; such petitions should be rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate circumstances to vacate include examples: (A) order not facially based on prior art patents or printed publications (e.g., ordered based on 35 U.S.C. 112), (B) all claims were held invalid by final federal court decision after appeals, (C) reexamination ordered for the wrong patent, (D) reexamination ordered based on a duplicate copy of the request. There is no right to petition as ultra vires if SNQ finding is based on reasons other than those urged by requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling third‑party opposition to 1.181 petition (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 is filed to vacate a reexamination order, a third‑party requester may file a single submission in opposition; because reexaminations proceed with special dispatch, any opposition must be filed within two weeks of service of the petition to ensure consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requester should consider notifying CRU support staff and the CRU SPRS by phone upon receipt and file opposition electronically when possible. The filing of a 1.181 petition is limited to a single submission even if an opposition is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art submitted after the order is not considered during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior art citations or written statements under 37 CFR 1.501 submitted after the date of the decision on the order are stored until the reexamination is concluded and will not be considered by the examiner during the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.502 and 1.902; submissions filed after an order are entered in the patent file but not considered in the reexamination (see MPEP §2206).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision denying reexamination — required explanations for each citation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request for reexamination is denied because no substantial new question of patentability is found, the decision must indicate, for each patent and printed publication cited in the request, why the citation is one of the following: (A) Cumulative, (B) Not available against the claims, (C) Not important to a reasonable examiner, or (D) Cited in the record and barred by guidelines in MPEP §2242 II.A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.02 as the introductory paragraph in a decision denying reexamination ('No substantial new question of patentability ... for the reasons set forth below'). Also respond to the substance of each argument raised by the requester which is based on patents or printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and effect of petition from denial (37 CFR 1.515(c) / 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester may petition the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 within one month of the mailing date of the examiner's determination refusing ex parte reexamination; any such petition must comply with §1.181(b). If no petition is timely filed or the petition affirms the denial, the determination is final and nonappealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRU Director's review of a petition is de novo. If the petition is granted, the decision should set a two‑month period for filing a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 and the reexamination file will be returned to the CRU SPRS of the art unit handling the reexamination for reassignment. A decision on petition is final and nonappealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassignment policy after petition/refusal to reexamine
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner's determination failed to find any SNQ and a petition is filed, reassignment of the reexamination proceeding to another examiner will be the general rule; under normal circumstances, the case will not be reassigned to a primary or assistant examiner who was involved in any part of the original examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be made only in exceptional circumstances (e.g., original examiner and denier are the only examiners with adequate knowledge of the technology). If reassignment occurs, it is typically to an examiner not previously involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund and file conclusion after petition period expires
rubrics_metrics.description: If no petition seeking review of the denial is filed within one month, the CRU processes the file as a concluded reexamination file and a partial refund of the filing fee for requesting reexamination will be made to the requester (per 37 CFR 1.26(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reexamination proceeding is given a 'concluded' status (420). Printed PDP screens are annotated 'PROCEEDING CONCLUDED' and scanned into IFW with appropriate document codes; the concluded reexamination file becomes part of the patent's record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner’s statement timing and content (37 CFR 1.530)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in §1.510(e), no statement or other response by the patent owner shall be filed prior to determinations under §1.515 or §1.520; the order for ex parte reexamination will set a period of not less than two months from the date of the order within which the patent owner may file a statement on the new question of patentability, including any proposed amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any statement must clearly point out why the subject matter as claimed is not anticipated or rendered obvious by the prior art patents or printed publications, either alone or in any reasonable combinations. A copy of the statement must be served on the requester (unless requester is the patent owner). If proof of service is omitted, CRU should contact patent owner to correct; absence of service after the two‑month period may render the statement inappropriate and it may be denied consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester reply period (37 CFR 1.535)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period for response by requester for a reply under 37 CFR 1.535 is two months from the owner’s service date and not two months from the date the patent owner's statement was received by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure service date is documented; requester’s two‑month reply period counts from service on requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of patent owner’s statement program
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner waives the right to file a statement in response to a request, the examiner may act on the first Office action on the merits immediately after determining reexamination will be ordered and may issue the reexamination order and the first Office action on the same day (or shortly thereafter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRU will contact the patent owner by telephone to request the optional waiver; discussion of merits is not permitted. Agreement/non‑agreement will be entered on the record using PTOL‑2292 (Interview Summary). Patent owner should not file a written statement of the communication as it will slow the process. If waiver agreed, examiner may issue order and first Office action together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.121(j) and 1.530(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the description and claims in patents involved in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with §1.530. An amendment paper must direct specified changes to the patent specification, including claims, or to the drawings, and may accompany a patent owner request or statement or be filed during prosecution where permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification changes: submit entire text of added/rewritten paragraph with markings per paragraph (f), or delete an entire paragraph by a deletion statement identifying the precise location. Claims: include entire text of each claim being changed and of each new claim; follow claim number with a parenthetical 'amended,' 'twice amended,' etc.; changed and added claims must include markings per paragraph (f), or cancel a claim by a canceling statement. Drawings: submit a sketch showing proposed changes in red for examiner approval; upon approval file new sheets in compliance with §1.84, identify amended figures as 'Amended' and new figures as 'New'; canceled figures bracketed and identified as 'Canceled.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims and support for claim changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims, supply on pages separate from those containing the changes the status (pending or canceled) as of the date of the amendment of all patent claims and of all added claims, and provide an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the changes to the claims made by the amendment paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear cross‑references to support in the specification for each amended or added claim; separate pages preserve clarity of status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking conventions for amendments (brackets/underlining) and claim numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes relative to the patent being reexamined which are made to the specification, including the claims, must include: deletions enclosed in brackets and additions underlined. Patent claims may not be renumbered; numbering of any claims added in reexamination must follow the number of the highest numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent markings per paragraph (f). Preserve numbering sequence; do not renumber existing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on amendments (no new matter / no enlargement / expiration)
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent. No amendment, other than cancellation of claims, will be incorporated into the patent by a certificate issued after the expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must be relative to the patent specification in effect as of the filing date of the request for reexamination. Proposed amendments are treated as entered in Office actions but are not effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require amendment of disclosure to secure correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Office finds inconsistencies or inaccuracies, require amendment to ensure the specification supports the claims and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements for papers (37 CFR 1.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers (other than drawings) submitted on paper or facsimile that are to become part of permanent USPTO records in the file of a patent application, reexamination, or supplemental examination must be on sheets of paper that are the same size, not permanently bound, flexible, strong, smooth, non‑shiny, durable, white, and either A4 or 8.5×11 inches with specified margins; written on one side in portrait orientation; plainly and legibly written by typewriter or machine printer in permanent dark ink; presented with sufficient clarity and contrast to permit reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheets should have no holes; pre‑printed Office form information and certain double column patent copies are exceptions. See §1.58 for chemical/math formulae/tables and §1.84 for drawings. Electronic submissions must comply with USPTO patent electronic filing system requirements.
